sentences.text: SENIOR
CIVIL JUDGE AND CJM DHARWAD IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE.
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER Petitioner who is arraigned as accused No.2 has filed this petition under Section 439 r/w Section 482 Cr.P.C, to release him on bail in Cr.No.251/2022, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420 r/w Section 34 I.P.C, urging the following:
GROUNDS (i) Petitioner belongs to Revenue Department and he was on deputation to KIADB,
Dharwad for two months.
The alleged incident occurred in between 07.01.2021 to 21.01.2021 and 09.07.2021 to 30.04.2022.
Petitioner took charge as SLAO, KIADB, Dharwad on 04.11.2022.

He was not working in KIADB,
Dharwad when the alleged incident took place.

(ii) In respect of the alleged incident a Committee was constituted and it has submitted report dated 14.12.2022 and additional report dated 19.12.2022, categorically stating that one Shankar Y.Talwar was SLAO from 2004 to 2018 and he was responsible for the illegal acts.
Based on it, KAT has stayed the suspension of petitioner.
While registering the FIR these facts are not taken into consideration.

For prosecuting the petitioner sanction is not secured as required under Section 197 Cr.P.C.
(iii) Petitioner was a resident of the address given in the cause title.
He undertakes to abide by any condition that may be imposed and prays to allow the petition.

2. In support of his arguments, learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the following decisions:
 (i) Jayaraj Vs. State of Karnataka & Ors.
 (Jayaraj)1  (ii) Ashoo Surendranath Tewari Vs.
The Deputy Superintendent of Police, EOW, CBI and Ors.(Ashoo Surendranath Tewari)2 Crl.A.No.575/2020(Arising out of SLP (Crl)No.5422/2015)

sentences.text: 3. In this regard learned counsel for petitioner has also relied upon order in Application No.11455/2022 dated 23.05.2023 passed by the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal at Belagavi, quashing the order of suspension on the ground that the order of suspension is passed without the prior permission of the lending department as required under the Rules.

entities.text: Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal at Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. Learned Addl. SPP submitted that the objections filed in Crl.P.No.100291/2023 and connected matters may be treated as objections to this petition also.

5. The objections filed in the said petition reveal that on 20.12.2022, complainant who is presently working as Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, Dharwad, has filed complaint stating that some of the owners of acquired land, though have already received compensation, have taken compensation for the second time in a total sum of Rs.19,19,55,000/- and this was done in collusion with some of the officials of KIADB and previous Special Land Acquisition Officer and other subordinate officials.
This was disclosed in the preliminary report.
5.1 Learned Addl.
SPP submitted that petitioner absconded and only after rejection of his petition for anticipatory bail, he was arrested.
The investigation is going on.

At this stage if released on bail,
petitioner may interfere with the investigation and also abscond and prays to reject the petition.

6. Heard arguments and perused the record.
7.

As evident from the complaint averments, complaint is given by Smt.Mamatha Hosagoudar,
presently working as Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, Dharwad.

Since there was allegation that in respect of acquisition of lands situated at Kelageri, Mammigatti and Kotur villages, double payments were made and this was possible due to the collusion of officials of KIADB, including SLAO V.D.Sajjan, M.K.Shimpi (petitioner), Shankar Y.Talwar and contract employee Hemachandra Chintamani.
A sum of Rs.19,19,55,000/- was paid for the second time, though already compensation was paid.

Based on the said preliminary report, complaint was filed not only against accused Nos.1 to 4, but also the beneficiaries who are arraigned as accused Nos.6 to 11 and the Bank staff who are arraigned as accused Nos.12 to 14.

The compensation is also granted in the name of one Madarsab Halabhavi, who is arraigned as accused No.5, but the investigation revealed that he had died long back and in fact he has sold his land and the purchaser has received the compensation and his name is made used to cheat KIADB.
8. During the pendency of the investigation, petitioner has absconded.
Only after his petition for anticipatory bail was rejected, he was arrested and investigation is proceeded with.

9. There are specific allegations against the petitioner that from 04.11.2021 to 27.12.2022, he has worked as Manager/Sheristedar at KIADB, Dharwad and one of the signatories to the file through which compensation was disbursed for the second time.
On 27.03.2023, petitioner was interrogated by the Investigating Officer and the investigation also reveal that he has maintained the note sheet and signed the RTGS form.
His sample handwriting is also collected for examination by the handwriting expert.
Again on 29.03.2023, petitioner was interrogated which reveal that he has handled the register in respect of the double payment made.

sentences.text: Only after his petition for anticipatory bail was rejected, petitioner was arrested.
The investigation is yet to be completed.
The charges leveled against the petitioner and others are very grave.
The offence under Section 409 I.P.C. is punishable upto imprisonment for life.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, the decisions relied upon by the learned counsel for petitioner are not applicable to the case on hand.
11. So far as the order in Application No.11455/2022 is concerned, the suspension order was quashed on the ground that the permission of the lending department was not obtained.
It is based on altogether different consideration than the grounds under which criminal proceedings are initiated.
The said order is not having any bearing on the present petition.
Therefore, no reliance could be placed on it.
12. So far as the contention of the petitioner that sanction order is not secured to prosecute him.
It is a premature stage to seek sanction.
Sanction would be secured only after the investigation is completed.
13. For the above reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that this is not a fit case to grant bail and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is rejected.
